recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-8826; separate reconciliation, if desired, should handle later Provenance correction/removal issues under their own Jira keys.
issue_request: FHIR-8826 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for DSTU2. It asked for a standardized way to flag historical resource versions as entered in error and resolved to document that Provenance should be used for a past version, that multiple Provenance instances may exist for a version, and that clients tracing history should retrieve Provenance for the resource or its versions. The resolution also distinguished whole-record entered-in-error status from documenting a historical version as erroneous.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by git-svn commit ea40a685d3c475a4d356d4aec37cdfd7dfbf2e61, '#8826 - notes about past history', corresponding to SVN build@8038 and the Jira comment. That commit added the HTTP history-page notes saying past versions cannot be updated or deleted, Provenance should point to a past version when it needs to be documented as entered-in-error, and applications tracing history should retrieve related Provenance resources.
additional_context: The current build retains the history-page guidance in source/http.html. The Provenance resource introduction now explicitly says Provenance can target any resource or version, including past versions, and that multiple Provenance records may exist for a resource or version. The current lifecycle page describes entered-in-error as a whole-resource state. Later R6 Provenance work, including FHIR-53917 and FHIR-53783, further refined correction/removal guidance and added a relevant-history profile and activity value set containing a NULLIFY/Mark Entered-in-error code, but those later Applied issues are separate Security WG changes and were not decided here.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already conveys the FHIR-8826 resolution through the active HTTP history page, active Provenance resource guidance, and current entered-in-error lifecycle summary.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied Security WG issue refined Provenance removal/replacement guidance and confirms current Provenance history modeling is broader than the original DSTU2 note.
Later Applied Security WG issue added a Provenance correction example for historical data with errors; it is separate from this FHIR-8826 audit.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive with Modification issue asking for historical records to be flaggable as entered-in-error using Provenance guidance.
evidence_items.learned: The final resolution establishes that Provenance, not an update to the historical version itself, is the intended mechanism.

evidence_items.summary: The HTTP history page says to use Provenance pointing to a past version when it needs to be documented as entered-in-error and to retrieve Provenance when tracing history.

evidence_items.summary: Provenance references may target any resource or version, including past versions, and multiple Provenance records may exist for a resource or version.

evidence_items.summary: The entered-in-error summary describes a whole-resource state for resources created accidentally and to be ignored.
